title: Backend contract: strong common shape without lowest-common-denominator pretending
summary: Backends publish identity, implementation kind, capabilities, limitations, requirements, qualification state and selection priority through a provider-neutral model. SUPPORTED, UNSUPPORTED, CONDITIONAL and UNKNOWN are distinct states. UNKNOWN or CONDITIONAL must not be silently promoted to SUPPORTED. A missing capability is an explicit eligibility failure, not an invitation to guess.
invariants: Capability status is explicit and machine-readable.
Limitations are published separately from capabilities so absence is not ambiguous.
Implementation identity records whether the route is OOREXX_NATIVE, FOREIGN_RUNTIME or PROCESS_BRIDGE.
Requirements and qualification evidence remain distinct from capability claims.
A provider-neutral API may expose richer provider metadata without flattening it prematurely.

provenance.claim: v0.2 publishes explainable planner semantics and current backend profiles; UNKNOWN/CONDITIONAL are not silently treated as supported.
